roleTypes.label: Enabling condition
roleTypes.definition: A circumstance makes a route possible. It does not by itself establish a hazard.

roleTypes.label: Unsafe control action
roleTypes.definition: An action or omission linked to its controller, hazardous context, and affected constraint.

roleTypes.label: Loss scenario
roleTypes.definition: An explanation of how control can become inadequate, including feedback and execution problems.

roleTypes.label: Hazardous state
roleTypes.definition: A system state that can produce a loss together with relevant environmental conditions.

roleTypes.label: Optional amplifier
roleTypes.definition: A factor that could strengthen a route but is not required in every version.

roleTypes.label: Loss
roleTypes.definition: An outcome stakeholders seek to prevent, kept distinct from its contributing causes.

roleTypes.label: Recovery
roleTypes.definition: A response re-establishes enforceable safety constraints within a specified boundary. Its success requires verification.

title: Screening, selective records, and persistent exclusion
summary: Can decisions and the records they generate entrench exclusion beyond effective correction?
scope: The hypothetical scenario connects employment screening with record suppliers, policing allocation, model updates, and independent redress. These functions belong to analytically distinct organizations. No single controller is assumed to command the whole system.
purpose: Protect access to employment, accurate and contestable records, and effective correction of repeated exclusion.
boundary: This is a bounded discrimination scenario, not an extinction pathway. Neither cited case establishes the combined employment–policing cycle.
numbering: 0 gives the context. 1.x identifies precursors, 2.x the loss-of-control event, and 3.x conditional consequences. R identifies a possible recovery outcome. These numbers locate scenario components. They are not STPA method steps or a measure of proximity to catastrophe. The return arrow represents feedback, not an extra observed incident.
bowtie: The centre is exclusion beyond effective correction. Downstream record feedback can renew earlier screening risk. Recovery interrupts that loop and repairs affected decisions.
schema: Losses, hazards, controls, unsafe actions, and scenarios are traced by IDs. This prospective analysis is separate from the retrospective case evidence.
limits: A fictional cross-institutional scenario is compared with a non-AI enforcement record and a mathematical study. Causal links between unemployment, enforcement, and future exclusion require independent evidence.

losses.title: Unwarranted loss of employment
losses.text: People lose work or income because unsuitable or inaccurate information governs a decision.

losses.title: Persistent discriminatory exclusion
losses.text: Repeated decisions entrench disadvantage and make effective redress inaccessible to an affected population.

hazards.title: Exclusion beyond effective correction
hazards.text: Consequential exclusion propagates through decisions while timely challenge and correction cannot constrain it.

hazards.title: Selective records treated as independent risk evidence
hazards.text: The system reuses records shaped by its own decisions without adequately accounting for selection or limits of use.

controllers.title: Employer / screening decision authority
controllers.responsibility: Approve or suspend consequential screening use and reconsider affected decisions.
controllers.feedback: Disputed-record notices, review outcomes, and independent checks of decision effects.
controllers.assumption: Decision authority remains able to change an outcome before it becomes irreversible.

controllers.title: Record supplier
controllers.responsibility: Match, update, and correct the records supplied.
controllers.feedback: Source corrections, identity discrepancies, and dispute results.
controllers.assumption: A corrected record reaches every recipient that continues to rely on it.

controllers.title: Enforcement allocation authority
controllers.responsibility: Set and revise patrol allocation and the collection of discovery records.
controllers.feedback: Allocation history, independently reported incidents, and local effects.
controllers.assumption: Discovered records depend partly on where enforcement looked.

controllers.title: Model and data steward
controllers.responsibility: Admit updates, correct selection effects, and bound reuse.
controllers.feedback: Data provenance, drift checks, and independent outcome observations.
controllers.assumption: A statistical correction may depend on assumptions that change in deployment.

controllers.title: Independent review and redress
controllers.responsibility: Require timely correction, suspension, or reconsideration.
controllers.feedback: Affected-person reports, audited records, and confirmation that instructions changed decisions.
controllers.assumption: A formal correction order must reach an actor able to enforce it.

controllers.title: Screening and allocation pipeline
controllers.responsibility: Apply approved data and decision rules within contestable limits.
controllers.feedback: Approved data, correction instructions, and limits on use.
controllers.assumption: Separate deployments may share records and create cumulative effects.

controlLoops.feedback: The pipeline reports affected decisions, disputed records, and the effect of suspension.
Recipients acknowledge correction and identify derived records that still retain the error.
Independent incident reports and allocation history reveal selective discovery.
Audits compare updated predictions with independently sampled observations.
Decision-makers confirm changed outcomes and unresolved cases.

constraints.title: Check record accuracy and fitness
constraints.text: Consequential screening must use correctly matched, current information appropriate to the decision.
constraints.test: Do identity, duplication, and update checks block a materially wrong record before use?
constraints.limit: Stale sources, mistaken identity, uncertain proxies, or incorrect matching can defeat the check.

constraints.title: Make challenge change decisions
constraints.text: Affected people must be able to obtain timely review that can suspend or change consequential exclusion.
constraints.test: Does a valid dispute reach a decision-maker and change the decision within the relevant window?
constraints.limit: Cost, delay, inaccessible notices, or an unempowered reviewer may make appeal ineffective.

constraints.title: Account for selective discovery
constraints.text: Updates must account for how earlier allocations shaped the records being learned from.
constraints.test: Does the proposed correction prevent feedback under changed reporting and discovery patterns?
constraints.limit: A correction fitted to the wrong discovery process can retain or introduce bias.

constraints.title: Bound reuse across decisions
constraints.text: Records and predictions must not be reused outside a demonstrated, appropriate purpose without review.
constraints.test: Can provenance and purpose restrictions prevent unsupported reuse across deployments?
constraints.limit: Copied data, proxy variables, and diffuse responsibility may evade the restriction.

constraints.title: Verify correction reaches outcomes
constraints.text: Recovery must verify corrected records, reconsidered decisions, and interruption of renewed feedback.
constraints.test: After correction, do downstream records and decisions change and remain corrected?
constraints.limit: Derived records, delayed propagation, or a continuing input loop can recreate the exclusion.

nodes.title: Records govern screening
nodes.text: Criminal-history or predicted-risk records influence consequential screening.
nodes.requires: Records are used in the decision and are unsuitable, inaccurate, or poorly contested.
nodes.mechanism: Reliance on a record can transfer its errors or untested assumptions into a decision.

nodes.title: Exclusion outruns correction
nodes.text: Exclusion becomes consequential while effective review or correction fails to constrain it.
nodes.requires: An adverse decision, material effects, and inadequate timely correction.
nodes.mechanism: A mistaken screening result can become a sustained loss when the correction process cannot change the outcome.

nodes.title: Selective enforcement shapes records
nodes.text: Where enforcement is allocated changes what it discovers and records.
nodes.requires: Allocation affects discovery. The employment-to-enforcement bridge remains separately unestablished.
nodes.mechanism: Selective observation can change recorded arrests without a corresponding change in underlying offending.

nodes.title: Records reinforce future decisions
nodes.text: Records shaped by earlier decisions feed later predictions and allocation.
nodes.requires: Updates reuse those records without an adequate selection correction.
nodes.mechanism: Learning from a deployment’s own discoveries can renew the initial pattern. Cross-domain reuse requires additional support.

nodes.title: Disadvantage persists
nodes.requires: Sustained exposure, cumulative effects, and failure of correction or exit.
nodes.mechanism: A recurrent process can make local losses persistent, but neither case establishes this full societal outcome.

nodes.title: Decisions and records corrected
nodes.text: Effective review corrects records and affected decisions and interrupts renewed feedback.
nodes.requires: Correction propagates, consequential decisions change, and recurrence is monitored.
nodes.mechanism: Recovery acts on the affected system and outcomes. Reinforcing a check is a separate change to a barrier.

unsafeActions.context: The record is materially inaccurate or unsuitable and the decision can cause exclusion.

unsafeActions.action: Does not propagate a verified correction
unsafeActions.context: Recipients continue to use the incorrect record in consequential decisions.
The relevant employment opportunity or effective remedy has already been lost.

unsafeActions.type: Applied too long or stopped too soon
unsafeActions.action: Continues an input correction after its assumptions fail
unsafeActions.context: Changed reporting or discovery processes make the update reinforce selective records.

scenarios.title: A record error survives the decision
scenarios.text: Decision-makers treat a record as current and correctly matched when it is not.
scenarios.unknown: The case does not establish automated future-arrest prediction.

scenarios.title: Redress cannot act in time
scenarios.text: A dispute does not lead to a timely changed decision.
scenarios.unknown: How often effective correction succeeds in the hypothetical system is unknown.

scenarios.title: Selective discovery becomes apparent risk
scenarios.text: Allocation changes discovery, and new records are reused without an adequate correction.
scenarios.unknown: Transfer from the mathematical study to any particular deployment requires testing.

scenarios.title: Corrected records are recreated downstream
scenarios.archetype: Control action not executed or ineffective
scenarios.text: A recipient retains derived data or a feedback process regenerates the same misleading pattern.
scenarios.unknown: Neither reviewed case demonstrates the entire employment–policing–exclusion loop.

limitingConditions.example: Correction reaches both the record and the consequential decision.
limitingConditions.question: Does a successful appeal actually change downstream use?

limitingConditions.example: A record is not available or authorized for cross-domain reuse.
limitingConditions.question: Does that boundary remain enforceable when copying becomes easier?

limitingConditions.example: Input correction matches the reporting and discovery process.
limitingConditions.question: How does protection change when that process shifts?

sources.title: Leveson & Thomas · STPA Handbook (2018)
sources.use: This source supplies the method for analyzing losses, hazards, constraints, control structure, contextual unsafe actions, causal scenarios, and leading indicators.

sources.title: UK Civil Aviation Authority · Bowtie elements
sources.locator: Hazard, top event, threats, consequences, preventive/recovery controls, escalation factors
sources.use: This source supplies the presentation vocabulary. A bow-tie hazard source and an STPA hazardous system state are not interchangeable definitions.

sources.title: Critch & Russell · TASRA
sources.use: This source presents a fictional cross-institutional hypothesis. It does not describe an observed causal chain.

sources.title: FTC · HireRight settlement announcement (2012)
sources.locator: Allegations about accuracy and disputes; settlement notice
sources.use: This source provides a non-AI screening comparison. Allegations and proposed settlement terms are not adjudicated findings.

sources.title: Ensign et al. · Runaway Feedback Loops in Predictive Policing
sources.use: This source provides mathematical and computational evidence for selective-data feedback and a correction within its assumptions.

targets.label: Criminal-record screening can exclude people from employment

assessments.scope: This case provides a narrow non-AI comparison for screening-to-employment exclusion. Future-arrest prediction and the subsequent self-reinforcing loop are not established.

trace.text: The FTC alleged materially inaccurate reports and employment denials.
Settlement terms addressed accuracy, access, and disputes.

barriers.title: Record accuracy checks
barriers.action: Identity matching, updates, and duplicate checks should stop materially wrong records before they affect screening.
barriers.efficacy: The FTC alleged inaccurate and wrong-person reports and resulting employment denials. The announcement is not an adjudicated finding.
barriers.durability: Faster screening or wider data reuse can propagate an error before it is corrected.
barriers.failure: Incorrect matching, stale sources, or delayed correction allow unsuitable records to remain in use.

reinforcement.proposal: Test record matching and correction propagation before consequential reuse.
reinforcement.test: Trace a corrected record through every recipient and verify changed decisions.
reinforcement.basis: This is an analyst proposal. The case did not evaluate it.

view.failureRoute: Wrong or outdated records reach employers

reach.local: The FTC alleged that inaccurate, duplicated, and wrong-person criminal records caused employment denials. The proposed settlement included accuracy and dispute-handling obligations, without an admission of violation.
reach.systemic: This case provides a narrow non-AI comparison for screening-to-employment exclusion. Future-arrest prediction and the subsequent self-reinforcing loop are not established.

targets.label: Enforcement-generated records can reinforce a prediction

assessments.scope: This study provides a comparison for the record-feedback component only. Employment loss and deprivation causing new arrests were not tested.

trace.text: The model linked patrol allocation to discovered incidents.
Reusing these records produced a feedback loop.
The proposed correction prevented the modeled runaway loop.

barriers.title: Correction for enforcement-generated data
barriers.action: The study changed inputs to account for selective discovery.
barriers.efficacy: The correction prevented runaway feedback under its assumptions.
barriers.durability: Real reporting and discovery processes must match those assumptions.
barriers.failure: Distribution changes can invalidate the correction.

view.failureRoute: Distribution changes can invalidate the correction

dependencies.label: Model assumptions
dependencies.assessment: Real reporting and discovery processes must match those assumptions.

reinforcement.label: Selection-bias audit
reinforcement.proposal: Audit whether correction assumptions match reporting and discovery in deployment.
reinforcement.test: Compare independent observations and subgroup outcomes before treating the model correction as effective.
reinforcement.basis: This is an editorial proposal. Its effectiveness is unassessed.

reach.local: The study shows how police-discovered records can reinforce deployment to the same areas. Its input correction prevents the modeled runaway feedback. Reported incidents alone do not fully remove it.
reach.systemic: This study provides a comparison for the record-feedback component only. Employment loss and deprivation causing new arrests were not tested.

conditions.H-01:2: If exclusion becomes effective before correction
conditions.H-01:3: Only with additional allocation and discovery conditions
conditions.H-01:4: If selective records are reused without adequate correction
conditions.H-01:5: If exclusion recurs and redress remains ineffective
conditions.H-01:R: If correction reaches records and decisions

presentation.fidelity: Two component comparisons inform this bounded model. Neither establishes the combined hypothetical loop. Recovery is an alternative outcome, not a stage leading to further exclusion.

HRI-2012.title: HireRight screening case
HRI-2012.observed: The FTC alleged that inaccurate background reports led to employment denials.
HRI-2012.notEstablished: The announcement does not establish AI arrest prediction or the subsequent feedback loop. Allegations were not adjudicated findings.
HRI-2012.limit: This case supports a comparison between inaccurate screening records and employment exclusion.

record-accuracy.title: Record accuracy checks
record-accuracy.result: The FTC alleged material failures in record checks.
record-accuracy.conditionBasis: Broken describes the alleged checking failures in this account. It is not a judicial finding.
record-accuracy.strongerAI: More rapid screening and easier data reuse could spread an error before correction. Better matching could help. Test correction speed and downstream decisions.

reinforcement.proposal: Verify identity, currency, and correction propagation before consequential reuse.
reinforcement.test: Does a corrected record change every affected decision within the useful time window?

tentative.question: Could disputed records keep shaping later automated decisions?
tentative.basis: The FTC alleged inaccurate screening reports and failures to investigate disputes.
tentative.unresolved: The case does not establish AI use or a feedback loop. We would need to trace whether disputed records were reused and whether they continued to affect later decisions.

PFL-2018.title: Predictive-policing feedback study
PFL-2018.observed: An input correction prevented runaway feedback within the study’s model.
PFL-2018.notEstablished: The study did not establish effects on employment or show that its correction works across real deployments. It did not demonstrate an actual cycle of exclusion.
PFL-2018.limit: Protection depends on the study’s reporting and discovery assumptions.

PFL-2018-correction.title: Correction for selective discovery
PFL-2018-correction.result: The corrected model avoided the runaway loop.
PFL-2018-correction.conditionBasis: Holding and reinforced apply to the corrected mathematical setup, relative to its uncorrected baseline.
PFL-2018-correction.strongerAI: Protection is brittle to incorrect assumptions about discovery and reporting. More adaptive allocation could change those processes. The correction must be retested.

reinforcement.proposal: Check selection assumptions against independent observations and outcomes.
reinforcement.test: Does the correction still prevent feedback when reporting and discovery patterns change?

tentative.question: Could the modeled feedback produce persistent disadvantage in practice?
tentative.basis: The study demonstrates how discovered records can reinforce repeated allocation and tests an input correction.
tentative.unresolved: The study did not establish long-term effects on people. We would need deployment evidence showing whether selective records repeatedly change decisions and whether those decisions sustain disadvantage.

context.title: System setting
context.text: The hypothetical scenario connects employment screening with record suppliers, policing allocation, model updates, and independent redress. These functions belong to analytically distinct organizations. No single controller is assumed to command the whole system.

targets.label: Records
targets.text: Employment screening depends on record suppliers.

targets.label: Allocation
targets.text: Policing allocation and model updates are analytically distinct functions.

targets.label: Redress
targets.text: Independent redress spans organizations. No single controller commands the whole system.

cloud.summary: What gets recorded depends partly on where enforcement looks. Those records can travel to other decision-makers, while correction must cross the same organizational boundaries.
